the sync login export reaches the engine's SyncLogin, method 3 of the sync service, through the dispatcher; at another method the owner's password would go to an engine call the export does not mean, and a reader would lose which method the login is pinned to (SPEC-364 B6)

the normal sync export reaches the engine's SyncCollection, method 5 of the sync service, through the dispatcher; at another method the host key would go to an engine call the export does not mean, and a reader would lose which method the sync is pinned to (SPEC-364 B6)

the normal sync from the Worker asks for no media, which the core refuses until media sync lands; asking for media would turn every browser sync into a refusal, and a reader would lose that the export never asks for it (SPEC-364 B6)

an engine refusal reaches the Worker as the engine's own error bytes, which the credential module classifies to tell a refused key from a lost network; a text in their place would read every refusal as offline and keep a refused key, and a reader would lose the bytes the classification needs (SPEC-364 B6)

the sync login answers the host key the engine returned, which the Worker seals and sends on each sync; an empty answer would store a key no server accepts, and a reader would lose that the export hands the engine's key back (SPEC-364 B6)
